title: ORIGINAL FRUIT BOX LABELS
reason: Large collection of original fruit crate labels (Tasmanian, NSW, Canadian and Washington State), many apparently unused stock, in albums; a collectors' niche and the quantity is unknown.
findings: Photos show about three spiral-bound albums or folders holding labels in plastic sleeves, plus at least eight loose stacks of crisp labels that look unused. Legible labels: LALLA Brand Fancy Apples in gold foil and white versions ('Produce of Tasmania Australia', 'Grown and packed by W.A.G. Walker & Sons, Riverside, Tamar Valley, Tasmania', blue 'Quality' seal); 'Fancy Pears' labels in blue and green; magenta and white labels reading 'TAS FRU...' (partly legible) with a stylised F and leaf; a 'Southern Isle Pre-cooled Tasmania' card or album cover; DOLLAR BIRD APPLES 'Selected for Export' (The Producers Co-operative Distributing Society Ltd, Sydney NSW, and at Leeton, Kentucky, Adelaide, Brisbane, Devonport (Tas), Melbourne); BLUE BIRD Canadian Products (Distributors Sales Service Limited, Kelowna BC, packed and shipped by Crown Fruit Co. Ltd, Kelowna, with an Empire star); TWIN W Brand (Wells & Wade Fruit Company, Wenatchee, Washington, contents 40 lbs net); and BUY ME Brand Canadian Apples ('Volume bushel', tiny foot imprint that looks like 'Litho'd in Canada'). The bright lithography and crisp edges suggest genuine printed stock rather than modern reprints, though this is not certain from photos. No dates legible. The quantity cannot be counted but is likely well over 100 labels. Fruit crate labels from Tasmania, NSW, Canada and Washington State are a recognised collecting niche. I could not check market prices (web search budget was used up).
condition: Labels look bright and clean with sharp corners and the loose stacks look unused. Plastic sleeves have glare and a few creases; album covers are plain card or plastic with spiral binding. Backs of labels not shown.
rescore_note: Three albums of presentation labels (Lalla gold foil, Dollar Bird from NSW, Blue Bird and Buy Me from British Columbia, Twin W from Washington State) plus about eight loose stacks of crisp Tasmanian Lalla, pear and Tas Fruit labels that look like unused packing shed stock; Gowans Hobart recorded sale prices of $280 for a large quantity of apple labels (lot 439367, https://www.gowansauctions.com.au/backend/api/v1/lots/439367/) and $440 for 16 original Tasmanian apple labels (lot 439391, https://www.gowansauctions.com.au/backend/api/v1/lots/439391/), both listed 20 Sep 2026 and checked 19 Oct 2026, so my estimate is about $200 to $400.
